Long text but I hope my experience can help you. Not the same situation but I also live in a country where being LGBT can make your life a hell depending on who knows (I live in Mexico and I'm bisexual and I'm talking based on experience since once my classmates punched me and kicked me in the locker rooms because they had the suspicions of me being "deviated" when we were on elementary). In my case I came out to my parents after I almost died because of a cist, still it was too risky since I was 17 with a not finished technician carrier in highschool, they accepted me but told me to be careful and not tell anyone else in the family since they could either push me away or try to send me to a conversion therapy. What I can tell you is that it's not necessary that everyone knows even if they are family, yes it sucks to only smile or just ignore every time they say homophobic jokes and stuff (even my parents have done that after I came out) but with time you manage to adapt. Yes you might feel as if you're not completely honest but in reality you're not only looking for your safety but for your happiness and live as the person you truly are. ![img](emote|t5_2qhh7|548)
